attributes.body:
いたす, or 致（いた）す as it is often written, is a humble speech う-Verb, which refers to the actions of the speaker (or people within the speakers inner circle, like their company). Similarly to お〜する, いたす means 'to do'.

In the case of する verbs themselves, simply replace する with いたす. For other verbs, add いたす to the ます stem of the verb, while attaching お, or ご to the beginning (depending on whether it is a word of Japanese or Chinese origin).

Caution

Words that include the kanji 拝（はい） 'to worship', or 'to revere', do not usually require お, ご, or いたす. This is due to the word itself being 'respectful'.

Fun Fact

いたす is considered to be slightly more humble than お〜する, which means that it will be heard more frequently in advertisements, or being used by company employees.

attributes.source: [DBJG] A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar

attributes.body: Both いたす and する express performing an action, similar to the English 'do.' The key difference is politeness: する is the standard, neutral term used in everyday contexts, while いたす is a humble expression used to show respect by 'lowering' your actions (or those of your in-group) in relation to another person.

These are both humble forms used to describe one's own actions politely. お～する is used with regular verbs, such as 手伝う 'help' becoming お手伝いする (same meaning, but in a deferential sense). In contrast, いたす is the humble form of する and is used instead of お～する when using する itself. For example, 連絡いたします 'I will contact you.' is the humble form of 連絡する (same meaning).

second_relatable.title: お〜する
second_relatable.meaning: I humbly do, I am obliged to do, Humble speech

attributes.body: いたす is the humble form of する, used when talking about your own actions to someone respected. For example, 連絡いたします means 'I'll contact you.' in a deferential way. なさる is the opposite: the honorific form used when referring to the respected person's actions, as in ゴルフをなさいます ('He/she plays golf.').
